motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Jay Johnson to a One-Year Term to the Community Services Board begin…
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the appointment of Jay Johnson to a One-Year Term to the Community Services Board beginning April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027 . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Jay Johnson gets a one-year board term
motions.summary: The council appointed Jay Johnson to a one-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2027.
motions.impact: The shortest of the terms handed out that night, and the last seat filled. Nobody outside the board is touched by it.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of ShaRee Curtis to a Two-Year Term to the Community Services Board beg…
motions.motion: Councilmember Huish moved to approve the appointment of ShaRee Curtis to a Two-Year Term to the Community Services Board beginning April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2028 . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: ShaRee Curtis gets a two-year board term
motions.summary: The council appointed ShaRee Curtis to a two-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2028.
motions.impact: Volunteer seat, two years, no cost or change to residents.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Charlotte Ducos to a Two-Year Term to the Community Services Board b…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the appointment of Charlotte Ducos to a Two-Year Term to the Community Services Board beginning April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2028 . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Charlotte Ducos gets a two-year board term
motions.summary: The council appointed Charlotte Ducos to a two-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2028.
motions.impact: Staggered terms keep the board from turning over all at once. That is the whole effect of this one.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Steve Conger to a Three -Year Term to the Community Services Board b…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the appointment of Steve Conger to a Three -Year Term to the Community Services Board beginning April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2029 . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Steve Conger appointed to Community Services
motions.summary: The council appointed Steve Conger to a three-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2029.
motions.impact: Another advisory seat filled for three years. Day to day, you will notice nothing.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Jessie Southworth to a Three -Year Term to the Community Services Bo…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the appointment of Jessie Southworth to a Three -Year Term to the Community Services Board beginning April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2029 . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Jessie Southworth appointed to Community Services
motions.summary: The council appointed Jessie Southworth to a three-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2029.
motions.impact: A volunteer seat gets an occupant. There is no change to any city service attached to it.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Debra Kimbrough to a Three -Year Term to the Senior Advisory Board b…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the appointment of Debra Kimbrough to a Three -Year Term to the Senior Advisory Board beginning April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2029 . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Debra Kimbrough joins the Senior Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Debra Kimbrough to a three-year term on the Senior Advisory Board, running April 2026 through March 2029.
motions.impact: One seat filled on a volunteer board. Residents feel nothing from the appointment itself.

motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote, covering the routine items grouped there.
motions.impact: Consent items are the ones no councilmember flagged for discussion. Nothing here reaches your street or your bill.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah Approving the 5th Amendment to the Amended and Restated Overland Master Development Agreement and to bring it back at a future City Council meeting
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah Approving the 5th Amendment to the Amended and Restated Overland Master Development Agreement and to bring it back at a future City Council meeting . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Overland development change delayed
motions.summary: The council postponed the fifth amendment to the Overland master development agreement and will take it up at a later meeting.
motions.impact: Terms for building out Overland stay as they are for now. If you live near it or are following what gets built there, the decision is still open.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Professional Services Agreement with Economic & Planning Systems, Inc. for Consulting Related to Eagle's Landing. This item relates to Item 17.A. No formal discussion took place, as the applicant had addressed questions during the previous item. This item pertains to the City’s evaluation of a large regional commercial project along Pony Express Parkway, just north of the downtown area. The project is anticipated to utilize a TIF bond to finance off -site infrastructure, which requires a market study to evaluate factors such as absorption potential and market demand. In consultation with LRB Public Finance Advisors, Eco nomic & Planning Systems, Inc. (EPS) was selected to conduct the study, which is expected to take 1–3 months to complete.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Professional Services Agreement with Economic & Planning Systems, Inc. for Consulting Related to Eagle's Landing . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Market study hired for Eagle's Landing
motions.summary: The council hired Economic & Planning Systems to study demand for Eagle's Landing, a large commercial project on Pony Express Parkway north of downtown.
motions.impact: The study takes one to three months and feeds a decision on whether to use a TIF bond for roads and utilities there. Nothing breaks ground yet.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.60 and 17.10 regarding Fencing . There was no second to the motion, and it died for lack of a second
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.60 and 17.10 regarding Fencing . There was no second to the motion, and it died for lack of a second.
motions.headline: Move to reject the fence rules got no second
motions.summary: A motion to turn down the fencing code changes outright failed when no other councilmember seconded it.
motions.impact: The rejection never came to a vote, so nothing was settled here. The fencing question moved forward under a different motion the same night.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 17.60 and 17.10 regarding fencing and to bring it back for consideration at a future work session
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 17.60 and 17.10 regarding fencing and to bring it back for consideration at a future work session . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Fence rule changes put on hold
motions.summary: The council set aside proposed changes to the city's fencing rules and sent them back for a future work session.
motions.impact: Current fence rules stay in place. If you were waiting to see whether the limits on your fence would change, the answer is not yet.

motions.item_title: Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as QTS -SCL 2 as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Huish moved to adopt a n Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as QTS -SCL 2 as presented . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rezone the land known as QTS-SCL 2
motions.summary: The council approved a zoning change for the land known as QTS-SCL 2; the motion does not state the acreage or the new zoning.
motions.impact: The change resets what can legally be built on that property. The record here does not say where the land is or what the new zoning allows.

motions.item_title: Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 15.80, 17.10, 17.25, 17.100 regarding Slope Development , with a correction to change the misspelled word “fist” to “first.” Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a n Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 15.80, 17.10, 17.25, 17.100 regarding Slope Development , with a correction to change the misspelled word “fist” to “first.” Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for building on steep slopes
motions.summary: The city rewrote four sections of its code governing development on steep slopes, changing how hillside land may be built on.
motions.impact: If you own hillside land or plan to build on a slope, the rules for what you can put there have changed. Residents on flatter ground are unaffected.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule regarding Site Plan Amendments
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule regarding Site Plan Amendments . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change the fee for site plan amendments
motions.summary: The council amended the city fee schedule to change what it charges for site plan amendments; the motion does not state the new amount.
motions.impact: This touches builders and businesses that want to change an already-approved site plan, not ordinary homeowners. The record does not say what the fee now costs.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 2.65 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Establishing a Senior Citizens Advisory Board .
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt a n Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 2.65 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Establishing a Senior Citizens Advisory Board . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New advisory board for older residents
motions.summary: The council created a Senior Citizens Advisory Board in city code, giving older residents a standing group to advise the city.
motions.impact: If you are a senior in Eagle Mountain, there is now a formal channel to raise concerns to the council. The board advises; it does not decide.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the Development Agreement with Williams .
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a n Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah , approving the Development Agreement with Will -Power UT, LLC, conditioned on the following amendments to the agreement being made: 1. Clarify that only simple cycle natural gas technology may be used; and 2. Amend the additional property section to limit its use to the Stadion LLC parcel subject to the development agreement approved in October 2025; and 3. Amend the Timing and Rate of Development Section to require that the Generation Project be operational within five (5) years of the effective date of the agreement with the possibility of requesting an extension; and 4. That trees be planted along Pony Express Parkway in compliance with Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.35.080 . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Gas power plant approved on Pony Express Parkway
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Will-Power UT for a natural gas power plant, limited to simple-cycle technology and required to be running within five years.
motions.impact: A gas-fired power plant is now cleared to be built, with trees required along Pony Express Parkway. If you live nearby, expect construction within the next five years unless the company gets an extension.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting America250 Utah and Recognizing and Approving the Eagle Mountain Utah250 Community Committee .
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting America250 Utah and Recognizing and Approving the Eagle Mountain Utah250 Community Committee . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Backing for the 250th anniversary committee
motions.summary: The council endorsed America250 Utah and recognized a local committee to plan Eagle Mountain's part in the nation's 250th anniversary.
motions.impact: A volunteer committee now has the city's blessing to organize commemorations. Watch for events, but this resolution itself spends nothing and asks nothing of you.

motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved that studying bit coin as a method of payment to the City be added to the Legislative Priorities List . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to study accepting bitcoin for payments
motions.summary: The council added a study of bitcoin as a way to pay the city to its list of legislative priorities.
motions.impact: Nothing changes at the utility billing counter for now. This puts the question on a list to look into, not into practice.
